title: POC scoping: hosted vs dedicated vs private - Solace Finance
summary: Initial POC scoping call to decide between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment for Solace Finance. Key items: define success criteria (latency, cost, accuracy), size workload (qps, avg tokens, peak), set benchmark plan and timeline, and review security needs (SOC2, SSO, KMS, VPC). Action: Redwood to send pricing, security docs, and set up a benchmark run. Customer to provide sample workload and SLOs.
header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Redwood: Maya Chen (AE), Devon Patel (SE)
Customer: Alex Rivera (Head of ML), Priya Nair (CTO), Samir Gupta (Infrastructure)
Recording: Fireflies.ai auto transcript
Notes: deck shared (link), benchmark sheet link mentioned
action_items: Maya Chen - Send detailed pricing sheet (hosted per-token, dedicated committed tiers, private licensing) - due 2026-10-02
Devon Patel - Share benchmark run plan and request for sample prompts + tokens distribution - due 2026-10-01
Samir Gupta - Provide representative sample workload and peak qps numbers (CSV or S3 link) - due 2026-10-01
Maya Chen - Share SOC 2 and security compliance pack + KMS integration note - due 2026-10-03
Alex Rivera - Confirm target latency SLOs and quality metrics for the evaluation - due 2026-10-01
next_steps: Redwood to run a 2-week benchmark on hosted with customer's sample traffic (dev keys) and return 95/99p latency + cost estimate
Schedule technical deep-dive for Dedicated sizing with infra team (Devon + Samir) week of 2026-10-05
Customer to review security docs and confirm whether VPC/private deployment needed for POC (decision by 2026-10-08)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. Quick intro, I’m Maya on the account team, Devon is our SE who’ll run the bench stuff.
[00:15] Alex (Head of ML): Hi all, Alex here, so we want to scope a POC to figure out which deployment mode makes sense for Solace. We have some compliance constraints.
[00:30] Priya (CTO): Hey, Priya. Main ask is: low latency for customer-facing flows, and we can't send PII off-prem for certain customers.
[00:45] Devon (SE): Got it, thanks. Quick clarifying q: when you say low latency, are you targeting sub-200ms for short prompts or is it more like <500ms?
[01:05] Priya: Ideally <300ms 95th for the primary flow, but for longer context it's okay to hit up to 800.
[01:25] Samir (Infra): For network, we have VPC peering options and a strict firewall policy, and we require KMS-managed keys for any hosted integration if we store logs.
[01:40] Maya: That’s helpful. Today’s call: confirm success criteria, get workload sizing, outline benchmarks and timeline, and discuss Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs.
[02:05] Devon: I'll start with workload questions — what's your expected steady-state qps for generation requests? And average tokens per request?
[02:25] Alex: Steady about 20 qps, peak 150 qps during batch processing windows. Avg tokens about 180 per user interaction, some events are 600 tokens.
[02:45] Devon: Cool. So for a hosted proof we can run a benchmark using those distributions. We'll look at latency percentiles and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:10] Priya: Cost is also a top consideration — don't want a surprise at scale. We also need deterministic SLAs eventually.
[03:25] Maya: Right. Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and easier to start POC, but Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and better latency predictability, Private gives full control for regulated customers but involves longer lead time.
[03:50] Alex: Can you quantify 'better latency predictability'? Like 95th drops by X?
[04:05] Devon: Ballpark, for similar GPUs, Dedicated with reserved pools eliminates noisy neighbor variability. For example, on our benchmarks a hosted instance might show 95p = 250-400ms for short prompts depending on load, while a Dedicated pool tuned for your workload can get 95p down to ~180-250ms. But exact numbers depend on model size, quantization, and batch behavior.
[04:40] Priya: What about cost delta? What are we looking at for sustained 20qps with peaks to 150?
[04:55] Maya: We'll send a pricing sheet. Roughly, hosted per-token might look cheaper at low volume, but at sustained high throughput Dedicated reserved capacity usually lowers unit costs. Private is highest up-front but good for compliance.
[05:15] Samir: Also need to confirm data retention. We can't have any customer PII logged in hosted unless encrypted and with KMS in our control.
[05:30] Devon: We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we can offer envelope encryption and limited retention, but for full KMS control Private or Dedicated with VPC options is recommended. Note: transcription autocorrect sometimes shows 'V-P-C' in our notes, ignore that.
[05:55] Alex: Ok. Next, benchmarks: what metrics will you run?
[06:10] Devon: We'll do 95/99 p latency, p50, throughput under different concurrency, token/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and a quality regression test with your sample prompts to ensure outputs don't degrade when switching quantized models. We'll also check cold vs warm KV cache behavior.
[06:35] Priya: Cache behavior is critical, our flows have heavy prefix reuse. Does Redwood do prefix or KV caching?
[06:50] Devon: Both — we have automatic prefix and KV cache options. In practice that can reduce token compute for repeated contexts by 30-60% depending on reuse. We'll simulate your session patterns.
[07:10] Alex: For quality, what model family would you recommend? We care about both instruction-following and finance-specific retrieval augmented responses.
[07:25] Devon: For finance workloads we often suggest a mid-sized LLM tuned for instruction following; for strict PII workflows we recommend private variants or fine-tuned models hosted on Dedicated or Private. We can test multiple model variants during the POC.
[07:50] Priya: Timeline: how long to get meaningful bench results?
[07:58] Maya: We can do an initial hosted benchmark in ~1 week once we have samples. Dedicated sizing and procurement might take 2-4 weeks more. Private deployment (on-prem) is several weeks to months depending on network and audit needs.
[08:20] Samir: For Dedicated, do you support colocated hardware or is it managed?
[08:30] Devon: Dedicated is Redwood-managed GPU pools reserved for you. We can set up VPC networking so traffic stays in your cloud account for ingress/egress. Private is the option if you want us to ship a package for on-prem or run in your VPC with a private control plane.
[08:52] Alex: Any friction for our infra team around SSO and RBAC?
[09:00] Maya: We support SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC across deployments. We'll include the SSO setup doc.
[09:15] Devon: Quick note on benchmarks: please provide token distribution histogram and a sample of 500 user sessions. That will let us create a realistic load profile and simulate prefix reuse.
[09:35] Alex: We'll export session data with redacted PII and upload to S3. Samir will own that.
[09:45] Samir: Yep I'll produce that. Also want to confirm audit logging retention and where logs live.
[09:55] Devon: For Dedicated and Private you control logging retention; for hosted we offer configurable retention and can push logs to your S3 or SIEM.
[10:10] Priya: Let's talk success criteria concretely: what are we measuring to call POC a success?
[10:20] Alex: From product side: 95p latency <300ms for standard flows, accuracy parity within 3% of current baseline on our evaluation prompts. From infra: predictable cost estimate and no blockers on compliance.
[10:35] Devon: I'll restate: 1) Latency target 95p <300ms for typical 150-200 token flows. 2) Quality regression <3% drop vs baseline. 3) Bench cost estimate within budget threshold — please provide that number. 4) Security checklist satisfied (SOC2 doc reviewed, KMS ok).
[11:00] Maya: What's the budget threshold?
[11:05] Priya: We have an internal bar — cost per MAU needs to be <= $0.20 incremental for this feature. We'll translate offline to per-token number and share with you.
[11:20] Devon: Good, that'll help us pick models and quantization strategies to meet cost target. We can run quantized variants in the bench.
[11:35] Alex: For bench runs, will Redwood simulate peaks to 150 qps?
[11:42] Devon: Yes, we'll simulate steady-state and peak bursts, including ramp-up. We'll report tail latency degradation and token consumption.
[11:55] Samir: Any need for privileged network access during bench?
[12:00] Devon: For hosted bench no special network access — we'll run from Redwood and you can run a traceroute. For Dedicated sizing we'll want a peering test if you plan to use VPC peering. For Private we'll need inside access to deploy the package.
[12:20] Priya: How do you handle data residency? Some customers require data never leave EU.
[12:30] Maya: We have regions in EU and NA; for hosted we can pin region, for Dedicated/Private you get full control. We'll capture residency needs in the security form.
[12:50] Alex: Ok. A few follow-ups: can you show a recent benchmark against a similar finance workload?
[13:00] Devon: Yes, I have a slide and a benchmark CSV we shared in the deck link. Note that the transcript may show a mis-typed model name 'Redwood Davinci' in the notes, it's 'Redwood-DaVinci'.
[13:20] Priya: Are there fallbacks in case Dedicated runs out of capacity?
[13:30] Maya: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to hosted or lower-cost model variants. Policies can be set to prioritise latency.
[13:45] Alex: For security review, will you provide a binding SOC2 report and pen-test summary?
[13:55] Maya: Yes, we'll attach SOC2 Type II and our pen-test executive summary. Private deployments can opt out of external logs if required.
[14:10] Samir: On KMS, we need customer-held keys for decrypting logs. Is bring-your-own-key supported on hosted?
[14:20] Devon: For hosted we offer envelope encryption; full customer KMS control is currently supported for Dedicated and Private. We'll document the differences in the security pack.
[14:40] Priya: Timeline recap?
[14:45] Maya: Ideal plan: you provide samples by 2026-10-01, Redwood runs hosted bench week of 2026-10-05 (1 week), then deep-dive sizing for Dedicated right after, decision on deployment mode by 2026-10-15. Private timeline depends on network and audit, estimate 4-8 weeks if chosen.
[15:10] Alex: Sounds good. Any blockers for sample share?
[15:15] Samir: We'll do an export, redact PII, and upload link. I need to confirm S3 bucket details with Devon.
[15:30] Devon: I'll share S3 upload instructions after call.
[15:40] Maya: Quick note on cost optimization: batching, caching, and quantization are the main levers. We'll propose config in the bench results.
[15:55] Alex: Great. Also want to see per-route cost breakdown in your console during POC.
[16:05] Maya: We can grant dashboard access for the bench so you can see per-route token cost, 95/99p latencies, and per-request traces.
[16:20] Priya: Excellent. Anything else we should add as success criteria?
[16:25] Alex: Also that we can automate rollouts and have canary fallback policies in the console.
[16:35] Devon: Yep, Redwood supports rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model or region. We'll demo that in the tech deep-dive.
[16:50] Maya: Alright, recap of action items and owners — we'll send those in email and in the CRM.
[17:05] Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll aim to have samples to you by 10/1.
[17:15] Alex: Thanks, bye.
[17:20] Maya: Thanks, bye everyone.
[17:30] [call ends]
